title: Смешанные условные предложения / Mixed conditionals
bridge: In Spanish, mixed conditionals combine tenses to express hypothetical situations across different time frames (e.g., past condition with present result). In Russian, this nuance is not expressed through a specific verb structure but rather through the combination of the particle 'бы' with different verb aspects and tenses, as well as context. The main challenge for Spanish speakers is that Russian does not have a direct correspondence between verb tenses and reality/irrealty; instead, the verb aspect (perfective/imperfective) plays a key role in shading the hypothesis.
rule: In Russian, conditionals are formed with the particle 'бы' (or 'б' after vowels), which is placed after the emphasized word or the verb. There is no special conjugation for the conditional; the past tense of the verb (both in imperative and context) is used followed by 'бы'. To express mixed conditionals (e.g., unreal past condition affecting the present), the past tense with 'бы' is used in the subordinate clause, and the present or future tense in the main clause, depending on the context. It is crucial to distinguish between perfective aspect (completed or punctual action) and imperfective aspect (ongoing or repeated action), as this determines the temporal interpretation. Examples: 'Если бы я знал (imperfective), я бы помог' (If I had known, I would help). For a past condition not realized that affects the present: 'Если бы я учился (imperfective), я бы сейчас говорил по-русски' (If I had studied, I would speak Russian now). There is no mandatory tense agreement as in Spanish; the interpretation is deduced from context. The particle 'бы' can appear at the beginning or after the subject/verb, but it usually follows the past tense verb. In subordinate clauses with 'если' (if), 'бы' typically comes after the verb; it is also used in the main clause. 'Бы' is used with past tense verbs, but it can also be used with infinitives in impersonal constructions (Надо бы...).

concept_examples.text: Если бы я знал, я бы пришёл.
concept_examples.translation: If I had known, I would have come.
concept_examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲi bɨ ja znal, ja bɨ prʲɪˈʂol]

concept_examples.text: Если бы он не опоздал, мы бы сейчас успевали.
concept_examples.translation: If he hadn’t arrived late, we would be on time now.
concept_examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲi bɨ on nʲɪ ɐpɐzˈdal, mɨ bɨ sʲɪjˈtɕas ʊspʲɪˈvalʲi]

concept_examples.text: Я бы купил этот дом, если бы у меня были деньги.
concept_examples.translation: I would buy this house if I had money.
concept_examples.phonetic: [ja bɨ kuˈpʲil ˈetət dom, ˈjeslʲi bɨ u mʲɪˈnʲa ˈbɨlʲɪ ˈdʲenʲɡʲɪ]

concept_examples.text: Если бы я был на твоём месте, я бы согласился.
concept_examples.translation: If I were in your place, I would agree.
concept_examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲi bɨ ja byl na tvɐˈjom ˈmʲestʲe, ja bɨ səɡlɐˈsʲilsʲə]

common_error.wrong: Если бы я знал, я пришёл.
common_error.correct: Если бы я знал, я бы пришёл.
common_error.explanation: The most common mistake is omitting the particle 'бы' in the main clause. In Spanish, both verbs carry the conditional marker (hubiera sabido / habría venido), but in Russian, it is mandatory to use 'бы' in both clauses to indicate unreality. However, in colloquial Russian, 'бы' is sometimes omitted in the subordinate clause if the context is clear, but it is always required in the main clause. Remember: 'бы' is the marker of unreality and must appear with every conjugated verb in the conditional.

examples.original: Если бы я был богатым, я бы путешествовал.
examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲi bɨ ja byl bɐˈɡatɨm, ja bɨ pʊtʲɪˈʂɛstvəvəl]
examples.translation: If I were rich, I would travel.
examples.note: The past tense of the verb 'быть' (был) with 'бы' is used to express an unreal present condition.

examples.original: Если бы она знала, она бы пришла.
examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲi bɨ ɐˈna ˈznalə, ɐˈna bɨ prʲɪˈʂla]
examples.translation: If she knew, she would come.
examples.note: Observe that the verb 'знать' is in the feminine past (знала) and 'бы' follows the verb.

examples.original: Мы бы пошли в кино, если бы был свободен.
examples.phonetic: [mɨ bɨ pɐˈʂlʲi v kʲɪˈno, ˈjeslʲi bɨ byl svɐˈbodʲɪn]
examples.translation: We would go to the cinema if he were free.
examples.note: In this sentence, the particle 'бы' is placed after the verb 'пошли' and also in the subordinate clause.

examples.original: Если бы я вчера сделал домашнее задание, я бы сейчас не сидел за компьютером.
examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲi bɨ ja ftɕɪˈra ˈsʲdʲeləd dəmɐʂˈnʲeje zɐˈdanʲɪje, ja bɨ sʲɪjˈtɕas nʲɪ sʲɪˈdʲel za kɐm⁽ʲ⁾ˈpʲjutʲɪrəm]
examples.translation: If I had done the homework yesterday, I wouldn’t be sitting at the computer now.
examples.note: The past with 'бы' (сделал бы) indicates an unreal past condition, and the present (сидел бы) expresses a present result.

examples.original: Если бы я не пошёл на вечеринку, я бы не встретил свою жену.
examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲi bɨ ja nʲɪ pɐˈʂol nə vʲɪtɕɪˈrʲinkʊ, ja bɨ nʲɪ ˈfstrʲetʲɪl svɐˈju ʐɨˈnu]
examples.translation: If I hadn’t gone to the party, I wouldn’t have met my wife.
examples.note: Here the past condition (не пошёл бы) has a past result (не встретил бы). It is not mixed, but a simple past conditional.

examples.original: Если бы я тогда был внимательнее, я бы сейчас понимал эту тему.
examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲi bɨ ja tɐɡˈda byl vnʲɪˈmatʲɪlʲnʲɪje, ja bɨ sʲɪjˈtɕas ponʲɪˈmal ˈɛtʊ ˈtʲemʊ]
examples.translation: If I had been more attentive then, I would understand this topic now.
examples.note: This is a mixed conditional: past condition (был бы) with present result (понимал бы).

levels.label: Выражение сожаления и совета (arrepentimiento y consejos)

examples.original: Зря я не купил билеты заранее, теперь бы я был на концерте.
examples.phonetic: [zrʲa ja nʲɪ kuˈpʲil bʲɪˈlʲetɨ zɐˈranʲɪje, tʲɪˈpʲerʲ bɨ ja byl na kɐnˈt͡sɛrtʲe]
examples.translation: I wish I had bought the tickets in advance, now I would be at the concert.
examples.note: Although there is no 'если', the particle 'бы' expresses an unrealized desire about the past with a present result.

examples.translation: You should have studied harder.
examples.note: 'Надо было бы' is used to express advice or regret about an unrealized past action.

examples.original: Если бы я был президентом, я бы подписал этот закон.
examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲi bɨ ja byl prʲɪzʲɪˈdʲentəm, ja bɨ pɐtpʲɪˈsal ˈɛtət zɐˈkon]
examples.translation: If I were president, I would sign this law.
examples.note: A present/future conditional with 'бы' and the past tense of the verb (был, подписал).

examples.original: Жаль, что ты не сказал мне, я бы помог.
examples.phonetic: [ʐalʲ, ʂto tɨ nʲɪ skɐˈzal mnʲe, ja bɨ pɐˈmok]
examples.translation: It’s a shame you didn’t tell me, I would have helped.
examples.note: The term 'жаль' (shame) introduces a feeling of regret, and 'бы' in the main clause marks the unrealized hypothesis.

title: Страдательный залог: инфинитив, деепричастие, модальные конструкции / Advanced Passive Voice: infinitives, gerunds, modals
bridge: In Spanish, the passive voice is formed with 'ser + past participle' and is often avoided using 'se'. In Russian, the passive is expressed with the verb 'быть' (only in past/future) and the short participle, or with reflexive verbs ending in '-ся'. For advanced learners, it's key to master the passive with infinitives (after 'мочь', 'нужно'), gerunds (деепричастия), and modal verbs like 'должен', 'приходится'. The typical error of Spanish speakers is to translate 'ser + past participle' literally using the verb 'быть' in the present (which doesn't exist), or to use the passive with 'быть' in constructions where Russian prefers the reflexive form. Additionally, the Russian gerund (деепричастие) has no direct equivalent, so learners must learn to express simultaneous or prior actions using specific forms.
rule:
In Russian, the advanced passive voice is constructed in several ways:
1. **Passive with short participle**: The short form of the past passive participle is used (e.g., 'сделан', 'написан') with the verb 'быть' in the past or future: 'Дом был построен' (The house was built). In the present, 'быть' is omitted: 'Дом построен' (The house is built).
2. **Passive with reflexive verbs in '-ся'**: Verbs like 'строиться', 'открываться' express the passive without an auxiliary: 'Дом строится' (The house is being built). This corresponds to the Spanish reflexive passive.
3. **Passive with infinitives and modals**: After modal verbs or expressions of necessity (можно, нужно, нельзя, должен, приходится), the passive infinitive (short participle or reflexive verb) is used: 'Работа должна быть сделана' (The work must be done).
4. **Passive participles**: Used as adjectives: 'прочитанная книга' (the book read).
5. **Gerunds (деепричастия)**: They do not have their own passive form, but the gerund of reflexive verbs is used to express the passive: 'будучи сделан' — though this is rare. More common is the form 'будучи + short participle' meaning 'being done'.

**Exceptions and pitfalls**:
- 'Быть' is not used in the present tense. 'Дом есть построен' is incorrect.
- With modal verbs, the passive is formed with the infinitive of the main verb in passive form: 'можно сделать' (it can be done) vs 'можно быть сделанным' (it can be done — less common).
- The passive gerund (деепричастие страдательного залога) is archaic and only used in elevated style. In everyday speech, it is avoided.
- Reflexive verbs in '-ся' are only used with inanimate subjects when the action is possible by itself: 'Книга читается легко' (The book is easy to read).

concept_examples.text: Эта работа должна быть сделана вовремя.
concept_examples.translation: This work must be done on time.

concept_examples.text: Дом был построен в прошлом году.
concept_examples.translation: The house was built last year.

concept_examples.text: Книга читается с большим интересом.
concept_examples.translation: The book is read with great interest.

concept_examples.text: Будучи приглашённым, я должен был пойти.
concept_examples.translation: Having been invited, I had to go.

common_error.wrong: Эта работа должна быть сделана быть вовремя.
common_error.correct: Эта работа должна быть сделана вовремя.
common_error.explanation: The error comes from a literal translation from Spanish 'debe ser hecho', adding 'быть' twice. In Russian, 'должна быть сделана' already includes the auxiliary 'быть' before the participle. Another more natural alternative is to use the impersonal construction 'нужно' + active infinitive. To avoid this, remember that passive constructions with modals are formed as 'должен/должна + быть + short participle', without repeating 'быть'.

examples.original: Это задание должно быть выполнено сегодня.
examples.translation: This assignment must be completed today.
examples.note: The structure is 'должно + быть + short participle'. 'Быть' is not used in the present tense, only in the past or future.

examples.original: Эту книгу можно прочитать за один вечер.
examples.phonetic: [ˈɛtʊ ˈknʲiɡʊ ˈmoʐnə prət͡ɕɪˈtatʲ zɐ ˈodʲɪn ˈvʲet͡ɕɪr]
examples.translation: This book can be read in one evening.
examples.note: In Russian, the impersonal form 'можно + infinitive' is preferred over the passive with 'быть'. It is more natural.

examples.translation: These documents cannot be touched.
examples.note: The modal 'нельзя' with the active infinitive expresses prohibition. The passive would be unnatural.

examples.original: Будучи написанной в спешке, статья содержала много ошибок.
examples.phonetic: [ˈbudʊt͡ɕɪ nɐˈpʲisənːəj f ˈspʲeʂkʲe, stɐˈtʲja sədʲɪrˈʐalə ˈmnoɡə ɐˈʂɨbək]
examples.translation: Having been written in a hurry, the article contained many errors.
examples.note: The form 'будучи + short passive participle' in the instrumental case expresses cause. It is formal and uncommon in everyday speech.

examples.translation: Having been invited, he did not come.
examples.note: The passive gerund is formed with 'будучи' + participle in the instrumental case. It is equivalent to the Spanish compound gerund.

examples.original: Прочитав книгу, он вернул её в библиотеку.
examples.phonetic: [prət͡ɕɪˈtaf ˈknʲiɡʊ, on vʲɪrˈnul jɵ v bʲɪblʲɪɐˈtʲɛkʊ]
examples.translation: Having read the book, he returned it to the library.
examples.note: This is an active perfective gerund, not passive. It is used for actions prior to the main verb.

examples.original: Проблема должна быть решена как можно скорее.
examples.phonetic: [prɐˈblʲɛmə dɐlˈʐna ˈbɨtʲ rʲɪˈʂɛnə kak ˈmoʐnə ˈskorʲɪjə]
examples.translation: The problem must be solved as soon as possible.
examples.note: The passive infinitive 'быть решена' is the standard form with modals. The short participle is used.

examples.translation: The documents can be signed tomorrow.
examples.note: With 'мочь', the infinitive 'быть' + short participle in plural is used.

examples.translation: This issue requires being considered.
examples.note: The verb 'требовать' takes the infinitive, and for the passive, 'быть + participle in instrumental' is used.

translations.en: Advanced Passive Voice: infinitives, gerunds, modals

title: Косвенная речь: сложные случаи / Advanced reported speech
bridge: In Spanish, when switching to reported speech, we change verb tenses (present to imperfect, etc.) and pronouns, but the structure is relatively flexible. In Russian, reported speech follows stricter rules: the introductory verb (сказать, спросить, etc.) determines the conjunction to be used (что, чтобы, ли) and the aspect of the verb in the subordinate clause. Additionally, personal and demonstrative pronouns systematically change according to the speaker's perspective, and the original tense is not maintained in the same way as in Spanish. A common mistake is to directly translate the Spanish structure 'dijo que + subjuntivo' into Russian, but in Russian 'чтобы' is used for commands and wishes, and 'что' for statements.
rule: In Russian, reported speech (косвенная речь) is formed using an introductory verb (говорить/сказать, спросить, ответить, etc.) followed by a conjunction and a subordinate clause. The conjunctions depend on the type of original speech: 1) Statements: 'что' (that) is used, and the subordinate verb can be in any tense, but the tense is adjusted to the moment of speech (there is no tense agreement as in Spanish). For example, 'Он говорит, что он болен' (He says he is sick) and 'Он сказал, что он болен' (He said he was sick). 2) Questions: if the question uses an interrogative pronoun (кто, что, где, когда, почему, как), that pronoun is maintained, and the word order is declarative (subject + verb). If it is a yes/no question, the particle 'ли' is used. Example: 'Он спросил, придёт ли она' (He asked if she would come). 3) Commands, wishes, and requests: 'чтобы' (so that) + infinitive (if the subject of the introductory verb is the same as that of the subordinate clause) or past tense verb (if the subjects are different) is used. Example: 'Он сказал мне, чтобы я пришёл' (He told me to come). Exception: if the introductory verb is 'велеть' (to order), the infinitive is more commonly used. There are also changes in personal and demonstrative pronouns: first and second person pronouns transform into third person according to context, and demonstrative adjectives (этот, тот) are adjusted to the new speaker's perspective. Time and place expressions also change: 'сегодня' becomes 'в тот день', 'здесь' becomes 'там', 'сейчас' becomes 'тогда', etc.

concept_examples.text: Он сказал, что уже купил билеты.
concept_examples.translation: He said that he had already bought the tickets.

concept_examples.text: Она спросила, придёт ли он завтра.
concept_examples.translation: She asked if he would come tomorrow.

concept_examples.text: Он попросил, чтобы я помог ему.
concept_examples.translation: He asked me to help him.

concept_examples.text: Мы знали, что он будет здесь.
concept_examples.translation: We knew that he would be here.

common_error.wrong: Он сказал, что он придёт завтра.
common_error.correct_alt: Он сказал, что он придёт завтра.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish, we often repeat the subject pronoun for clarity, but in Russian, if the subject is the same as that of the introductory verb, the pronoun is redundant and sounds unnatural. Additionally, when changing perspective, the pronoun sometimes needs to be changed: for example, if the original statement was 'я приду', when reporting it with 'он сказал', it must be 'он придёт', which is already implied in the verb ending. To avoid mistakes, check if the subject is the same and omit the pronoun if unnecessary. Also be careful with 'завтра', which does not change in Russian (unlike Spanish 'al día siguiente') if the same day is maintained; in a past context, it would be 'на следующий день'.

examples.translation: He says that he likes music.
examples.note: The present tense is maintained in the subordinate clause, unlike in Spanish where it sometimes changes to imperfect.

examples.translation: She said that she was at home.
examples.note: The past is expressed with the verb in the past tense; there is no need for pluperfect.

examples.translation: We found out that he had arrived.
examples.note: The perfective aspect 'приехал' indicates a completed action.

examples.translation: He asked where the library was.
examples.note: The interrogative pronoun is maintained, but the word order is declarative (subject + verb).

examples.translation: She asked if there was any bread.
examples.note: The particle 'ли' is placed after the word being questioned (here 'есть').

examples.original: Мы не знали, куда он ушёл.
examples.translation: We didn’t know where he had gone.
examples.note: The verb 'ушёл' is in the perfective past, indicating a completed action.

examples.original: Он сказал, чтобы мы ждали его.
examples.translation: He said that we should wait for him.
examples.note: With different subjects, 'чтобы' + past tense verb (жали – past of ждать) is used.

examples.original: Мама попросила, чтобы я убрал комнату.
examples.translation: Mom asked me to clean the room.
examples.note: The verb 'убрал' is in the perfective past, common in this type of construction.

examples.translation: He ordered her to come on time.
examples.note: With the verb 'велеть', the infinitive is usually used directly, without 'чтобы'.

title: Инверсия для эмфазы / Inversion for emphasis
bridge: In Spanish, to emphasize we often use structures like 'No solo... sino también' (Not only... but also) or 'Raramente...' (Rarely...), with inversion of the subject and verb. In Russian, word order is more flexible, and inversion is achieved by placing the emphasized element at the beginning of the sentence, while intonation and particles like 'только' (only) or 'не только' (not only) mark the emphasis. Unlike Spanish, where inversion is often mandatory in certain contexts, in Russian it is optional and depends on the register, but it changes the nuance of the sentence. Be careful: in Russian, the subject and verb are not inverted in the same way as in Spanish; instead, the order is altered to highlight a specific part.
rule: In Russian, inversion for emphasis is achieved by moving the element you want to emphasize (subject, object, adverb) to the beginning of the sentence. There is no fixed rule for subject-verb inversion as in Spanish (for example, 'Raramente vengo' -> 'Редко я прихожу'). The particle 'только' (only) or 'не только' (not only) is placed before the emphasized element. In negative sentences with 'ни... ни' (neither... nor) or 'не разу' (never), the negative adverb goes at the beginning, followed by the verb and the subject, similar to Spanish. The typical order is: [emphasized element] + [verb] + [subject] if the subject is new. For B2 level, it is important to use inversion in formal contexts (essays, speeches) and in sentences with 'так... что' (so... that) or 'такой... что' (such... that). Avoid excessive inversion in colloquial speech, as it can sound unnatural. Intonation plays a crucial role: the emphasized element receives the main stress. In sentences with 'не только... но и' (not only... but also), both emphasized elements go at the beginning, and the second part with 'но и' (but also) introduces additional information.

concept_examples.text: Не только он пришёл, но и его брат.
concept_examples.translation: Not only did he come, but his brother did too.
concept_examples.phonetic: [nʲɪ ˈtolʲkə on prʲɪˈʂoɫ, no i jɪˈvo brat]

concept_examples.text: Редко я видел такое красивое зрелище.
concept_examples.translation: Rarely have I seen such a beautiful sight.

concept_examples.text: Только позже я понял свою ошибку.
concept_examples.translation: Only later did I realize my mistake.

concept_examples.text: Никогда я не слышал такой чудесной музыки.
concept_examples.translation: Never have I heard such wonderful music.
concept_examples.phonetic: [nʲɪkɐˈgda ja nʲɪ ˈslɨʂəl tɐˈkoj tɕʉˈdʲɛsnəj ˈmuzɨkʲɪ]

common_error.wrong: Не только пришёл он, но и его брат.
common_error.correct: Не только он пришёл, но и его брат.
common_error.correct_alt: Пришёл не только он, но и его брат.
common_error.explanation: A common mistake is placing the verb immediately after 'не только' thinking that it inverts like in Spanish ('No solo vino él'). In Russian, 'не только' directly connects to the element it emphasizes (the subject 'он'), and the verb comes after. If you want to emphasize the action, you can place the verb at the beginning (Пришёл не только он...), but the subject must remain next to 'не только' when it is the emphasized element. To avoid this, identify which word is the focus: if it is the subject, place it after 'не только'; if it is the verb, place it after, followed by the subject.

examples.translation: Only mom knows this secret.
examples.note: 'Только' emphasizes the subject 'мама'. It is placed at the beginning, followed by the subject and the verb. In Spanish, intonation does the emphasis, but in Russian it is the word order.

examples.original: Только утром я почувствовал себя лучше.
examples.translation: Only in the morning did I feel better.
examples.note: 'Только' emphasizes the time adverb 'утром'. Here the inversion is partial: the adverb goes at the beginning, followed by the subject and the verb.

examples.original: Не только студенты, но и преподаватели были удивлены.
examples.phonetic: [nʲɪ ˈtolʲkə stʊˈdʲentɨ, no i prʲɪpədɐˈvatʲɪlʲɪ ˈbɨlʲɪ ʊdʲɪvˈlʲenɨ]
examples.translation: Not only the students, but also the teachers were surprised.
examples.note: Both emphasized elements (subjects) go at the beginning, connected by 'но и'. The verb 'были' agrees with the plural and comes after the second subject.

examples.original: Не только летом, но и зимой здесь красиво.
examples.phonetic: [nʲɪ ˈtolʲkə ˈlʲetəm, no i zʲɪˈmoj zʲdʲesʲ krɐˈsʲivə]
examples.translation: Not only in summer, but also in winter is it beautiful here.
examples.note: In this case, the inversion emphasizes the time adverbs. The copula verb 'есть' is omitted, and the order is: 'не только' + adverb + 'но и' + adverb + place + predicate.

examples.original: Никогда я не забуду этот день.
examples.translation: Never will I forget this day.
examples.note: The negative adverb 'никогда' goes at the beginning, followed by the subject 'я' and then the verb with 'не'. In Spanish, it is also placed at the beginning: 'Nunca olvidaré...'

examples.original: Ни разу я не был в Москве.
examples.phonetic: [nʲɪ ˈrazʊ ja nʲɪ ˈbɨɫ v mɐˈskvʲe]
examples.translation: Not once have I been to Moscow.
examples.note: 'Ни разу' (not once) at the beginning emphasizes total negation. In Spanish, it would be said 'Ni una vez he estado...' with a similar structure.

title: Эмфатические конструкции (Cleft sentences) / Emphatic constructions
bridge: In Spanish, to emphasize an element we use 'es... lo que', 'fue... quien', or simply word order with intonation. In Russian, there is no equivalent structure to 'It is... that', but the same effect is achieved using intensifying particles such as 'именно', 'же', 'ведь', and through flexible word order. The main difficulty for Spanish speakers is that in Russian emphasis is not marked by a fixed structure, but by particles and intonation, and word order is not entirely free: it depends on known (topic) and new (rheme) information.
rule: In Russian, to emphasize an element of a sentence, the following are mainly used: 1) The particle 'именно' (just, precisely) before the emphasized element: 'Именно Иван купил эту книгу' (It was Ivan who bought this book). 2) The particle 'же' (after all, indeed) placed after the emphasized element: 'Он же это сказал' (He was the one who said it). 3) The particle 'ведь' (after all, you know) to emphasize a known fact: 'Ведь это он сделал' (After all, it was he who did it). 4) Word order: the new or emphasized element is placed at the end of the sentence, breaking the SVO order. Example: 'Книгу купил Иван' (It was Ivan who bought the book – emphasis on Ivan). It is important to note that in Russian, unlike Spanish, no copular structure with 'that' is needed to emphasize; word order and particles are used instead. Additionally, particles do not change the declension of words: the emphasized element retains its grammatical case according to its syntactic function. For B2 level, it is crucial to master the combination of 'именно' with word order to express contrast and clarity in both formal and informal contexts.

concept_examples.text: Именно он купил эту книгу.
concept_examples.translation: It was he who bought this book.

concept_examples.text: Этот фильм я смотрел вчера, а не сегодня.
concept_examples.translation: This movie is what I watched yesterday, not today.
concept_examples.phonetic: [ˈɛtət ˈfʲilʲm ja smɐˈtrʲel ˈft͡ɕerə, a nʲɪ sʲɪˈvodʲnʲə]

concept_examples.text: Ведь это ты разбил окно!
concept_examples.translation: It was you who broke the window!

concept_examples.text: Жену я люблю, а не свою работу.
concept_examples.translation: It's my wife whom I love, not my job.
concept_examples.phonetic: [ʐɨˈnu ja lʲʊˈblʲu, a nʲɪ svɐˈju rɐˈbotʊ]

common_error.explanation: When translating 'it is... who...' literally, Spanish speakers tend to use 'это ... который', but in Russian this structure is used for explanatory relative clauses, not for emphasis. The correct way is to use the particle 'именно' before the emphasized element or rearrange the sentence. It is also common to place 'именно' after the noun: 'Иван именно купил книгу' – but this changes the nuance: it emphasizes the action, not the subject.

levels.label: Выделение с помощью «именно» / Énfasis con именно

examples.translation: It is us who have to do this.
examples.note: Именно is placed before the pronoun to emphasize who must do something.

examples.translation: He came precisely on Monday.
examples.note: Именно is used before 'в' to specify the day.

examples.translation: It is for this reason that I am calling you.
examples.note: Именно is used before 'поэтому' to emphasize the reason.

levels.label: Частицы «же» и «ведь» / Partículas же y ведь

examples.translation: He himself said it.
examples.note: The particle же comes after the element being emphasized; here 'он'.

examples.original: Ведь ты не знаешь этого правила.
examples.translation: After all, you don’t know this rule.
examples.note: Ведь introduces a fact the speaker considers known or obvious.

examples.original: Я же говорил, что не приду.
examples.translation: I told you I wouldn’t come.
examples.note: Here же reinforces the idea that it had already been said, similar to 'I already told you'.

levels.label: Порядок слов как средство выделения / Orden de palabras como recurso enfático
levels.translation: Word order as an emphatic resource

examples.original: Книгу я прочитал, а не журнал.
examples.translation: It was the book that I read, not the magazine.
examples.note: Placing the object at the beginning emphasizes it; contrast is highlighted with 'а не'.

examples.original: В Москве я был, а в Петербурге нет.
examples.translation: I was in Moscow, but not in Saint Petersburg.
examples.note: The adverb of place is moved forward to emphasize it; the second part uses 'а' to contrast.

examples.translation: This problem will be solved only by Sergei.
examples.note: The direct object comes first and the subject last, which is the position of emphasis.

title: Номинализация / Nominalization
bridge: In Spanish, we often use the infinitive as a noun (el correr, el pensar), but in Russian nominalization is much more productive and uses specific suffixes: -ение, -ание, -тие, -ость, -ство, -ка, etc. Unlike Spanish, where the derived noun often coexists with the nominalized infinitive, in Russian the infinitive is not used as a noun; you must choose the appropriate suffix. Be careful: some suffixes change the nuance (process vs. result), something that in Spanish is often expressed with articles or prepositions, but in Russian is expressed through the verb aspect and the choice of suffix.
rule: In Russian, verbs are nominalized by adding suffixes such as -ение/-ание (process or result: чтение, писание), -тие (событие, открытие), -ка (action with a colloquial nuance: уборка, выпечка), -ость (from adjectives: радость, скорость), -ство (quality or state: братство, бедство). Adjectives become nouns mainly with -ость (новый → новость), -ство (богатый → богатство), -ота (быстрый → быстрота), -изм (коммунизм). The verb aspect must be considered: the imperfective infinitive is normally used for the process (читание) and the perfective for the result (прочтение, though sometimes with nuances). Nominalization is frequently used in formal and scientific registers. There is no single rule, but there are common patterns: verbs ending in -ать/-ять often take -ание, those in -ить/-еть take -ение, and some are irregular (писать → писание, but идти → хождение). Nouns derived from adjectives can denote abstract qualities (скорость) or concrete entities (больной → больной as a noun, but this is full substantivization).

concept_examples.text: Чтение развивает мысль.
concept_examples.translation: Reading develops thought.

concept_examples.text: Уборка квартиры занимает много времени.
concept_examples.translation: Cleaning the apartment takes a lot of time.

concept_examples.text: Нам нужна быстрая обработка данных.
concept_examples.translation: We need fast data processing.

concept_examples.text: Его спокойствие нас удивляет.
concept_examples.translation: His calmness surprises us.

common_error.explanation: A typical error is using 'читание' because the verb is 'читать' and one might expect '-ание', but in this case the correct suffix is '-ение' (читать → чтение). It is a frequent irregularity. To avoid mistakes, you must memorize the suffixes for common verbs, paying attention to alternations and exceptions.

examples.translation: Education is an important factor.
examples.note: Verb 'образовать' → 'образование'. Suffixes -ание/-ение: process or result.

examples.translation: Victory requires effort.
examples.note: 'Победить' → 'победа' (irregular, does not use -ение).

examples.translation: The solution to the problem was found.
examples.note: 'Решить' → 'решение' (suffix -ение).

examples.translation: Running in the morning is beneficial.
examples.note: From 'пробегать' → 'пробежка' (concrete action, colloquial).

examples.translation: Doing laundry is a boring task.
examples.note: From 'стирать' → 'стирка'.

examples.translation: Replacing the part took an hour.
examples.note: 'Заменить' → 'замена' (also -ka in other cases, here -мена).

examples.translation: His bravery amazes everyone.
examples.note: From the adjective 'смелый' → 'смелость' (-ость).

examples.translation: The development of trade accelerated.
examples.note: 'Торговый' → 'торговля' (related to -ство, but irregular).

examples.translation: We value our brotherhood.
examples.note: 'Брат' → 'братство' (-ство: quality or state).

title: Модальные конструкции прошедшего времени / Past modal constructions (would have done, should have done)
bridge: In Spanish, you use the compound conditional or the imperfect subjunctive to express hypothetical actions in the past (habría venido, deberías haber llamado). In Russian, there is no direct equivalent; instead, modal verbs such as 'должен' (must), 'мочь' (can), and 'хотеть' (to want) are combined with perfective or imperfective infinitives, and nuances like regret or reproach are conveyed through verbal aspect and adverbs like 'надо было' (it was necessary). The main challenge for Spanish speakers is that in Russian, the modal is often conjugated in the neutral past (было) and the main verb remains in the infinitive without person agreement, and the perfective/imperfective aspect changes the meaning: 'надо было делать' (it was necessary to be doing) vs 'надо было сделать' (it was necessary to have done).
rule: In Russian, past modals are constructed with: 1) 'должен был' + infinitive (agrees in gender/number with the subject: должен был, должна была, должны были) to express unfulfilled obligation or likelihood. 2) 'надо было' / 'нужно было' + infinitive (invariable) to express necessity or advisability in the past, often with a nuance of reproach. 3) 'можно было' + infinitive for past possibility not realized. 4) 'нельзя было' + infinitive for past prohibition or impossibility. 5) 'мочь' in the past (мог/могла/могли) + infinitive to express past ability or permission. The aspect of the infinitive is crucial: imperfective indicates ongoing or habitual action, perfective indicates completed action or result. With 'надо было', the perfective (сделать) suggests the action was not done and is criticized; the imperfective (делать) suggests the action was carried out but not as it should have been or emphasizes the process. To express 'would have done' (conditional compound), 'бы' is used with the verb in the past: 'я бы сделал' (I would have done), and for 'should have done' 'надо было' or 'следовало бы' + perfective infinitive is used. 'Следовало бы' is more formal and used with бы for conditional. Examples: 'Я должен был прийти' (I should have come), 'Надо было позвонить' (you should have called), 'Можно было купить' (it could have been bought), 'Я бы сказал' (I would have said).

concept_examples.text: Я должен был прийти раньше.
concept_examples.translation: Debía haber venido antes / Debería haber venido antes.

concept_examples.text: Надо было позвонить ей вчера.
concept_examples.translation: Deberías haberle llamado ayer.

concept_examples.text: Можно было купить билеты заранее.
concept_examples.translation: Se podía haber comprado los billetes con antelación.

concept_examples.text: Я бы сделал это иначе.
concept_examples.translation: Yo lo habría hecho de otra manera.

common_error.wrong: Я должен был позвонить ей вчера, но я не звонил.
common_error.correct: Я должен был позвонить ей вчера, но я не позвонил.
common_error.correct_alt: Мне нужно было позвонить ей вчера, но я не позвонил.
common_error.explanation: The common mistake is using the imperfective aspect (звонил) in the main verb after 'должен был' when expressing that the action was not performed. In Russian, to indicate an unfulfilled obligation in the past, the main verb must be in the perfective aspect (позвонить) because it expresses a completed action that did not occur. If the imperfective is used, it suggests that the action was attempted or was in progress. Additionally, many Spanish speakers use 'должен был' with the verb in the past tense (звонил) by analogy with Spanish, but in Russian the main verb always appears in the infinitive.

levels.label: Модальные глаголы в прошедшем времени
levels.translation: Modal verbs in the past tense

examples.translation: Debía comprar pan / Tenía que comprar pan.
examples.note: Use of 'должен был' + perfective infinitive to express past obligation.

examples.original: Она могла прийти, но не пришла.
examples.translation: Ella podía venir, pero no vino.
examples.note: 'Могла' indicates past ability; the context shows it was not realized.

examples.original: Мы хотели пойти в кино, но было поздно.
examples.phonetic: [mɨ xɐˈtʲelʲɪ pɐjˈtʲi f‿kʲɪˈno, no ˈbɨlə ˈpoznə]
examples.translation: Queríamos ir al cine, pero era tarde.
examples.note: 'Хотели' + infinitive for past desire.

examples.translation: Deberías haber dicho la verdad.
examples.note: Perfective 'сказать' indicates the action was not done and is criticized.

examples.original: Нужно было готовиться к экзамену каждый день.
examples.translation: Había que prepararse para el examen cada día.
examples.note: Imperfective 'готовиться' emphasizes the process or habit.

examples.translation: No deberías haber hablado así.
examples.note: Negation with 'не надо было' for reproach.

examples.original: Я бы пришёл, если бы знал.
examples.translation: Habría venido si hubiera sabido.
examples.note: 'Бы' with the verb in the past forms the compound conditional.

examples.original: Она бы не опоздала, если бы вышла раньше.
examples.phonetic: [ɐˈna bɨ nʲɪ ɐpɐˈzdaɫə, ˈjeslʲɪ bɨ ˈvɨʂlə ˈranʲʂɨ]
examples.translation: Ella no habría llegado tarde si hubiera salido antes.
examples.note: Use of 'бы' in both clauses for hypothetical situations.

examples.original: Если бы я был на твоём месте, я бы согласился.
examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲɪ bɨ ja bɨɫ nə‿tvɐˈjɵm ˈmʲestʲɪ, ja bɨ səɡlɐˈsʲiləsʲ]
examples.translation: Si yo estuviera en tu lugar, habría aceptado.
examples.note: Unreal conditional with 'бы' in both parts.

translations.en: Advanced modals (would have done, should have done)

title: Деепричастия / Participial clauses
bridge: In Spanish, we use gerunds ('caminando por la calle, vi...') or subordinate clauses with 'mientras' to express simultaneous or prior actions. In Russian, this function is fulfilled by 'деепричастия' (Russian gerunds), which are invariable verb forms with specific suffixes (-я, -в, -вши). Unlike Spanish, the subject of the Russian gerund MUST match the subject of the main clause; otherwise, it is a serious grammatical error. Additionally, Russian does not use gerunds in passive constructions or with modal verbs like 'poder' or 'deber'.
rule: In Russian, деепричастия are formed in two ways: 1) **Imperfective** (simultaneous action): formed from the present tense of imperfective verbs by adding -я (after consonants or -а, -я after vowels) or -учи/-ючи (archaic). Example: читать → читая (reading). 2) **Perfective** (prior action): formed from the infinitive (or past tense) of perfective verbs by adding -в, -вши (after vowels) or -ши (after consonants). Example: прочитать → прочитав (having read). There is also the form -вши (rare but used in colloquial speech). Exceptions: some verbs do not form imperfective gerunds (e.g., писать, бежать, хотеть) or form them irregularly (e.g., быть → будучи). Golden rule: the subject of the gerund must be the same as that of the main clause. In the negative, use не + gerund. Gerunds are mainly used in written style (literary, journalistic); in colloquial speech, constructions with 'когда' or 'пока' are preferred.

concept_examples.text: Идя по улице, я увидел друга.
concept_examples.translation: Walking down the street, I saw a friend.

concept_examples.text: Прочитав книгу, он вернул её в библиотеку.
concept_examples.translation: Having read the book, he returned it to the library.
concept_examples.phonetic: [prət͡ɕɪˈtaf ˈkʲnʲiɡʊ, on vʲɪrˈnuɫ jɪˈjɵ v bʲɪblʲɪɐˈtʲekʊ]

concept_examples.text: Не зная языка, трудно жить в другой стране.
concept_examples.translation: Without knowing the language, it is difficult to live in another country.
concept_examples.phonetic: [nʲɪ ˈznajə jɪzɨˈka, ˈtrudnə ˈʐɨtʲ v ˈdruɡəj ˈstranʲe]

common_error.wrong: Идя по улице, окна были открыты.
common_error.correct: Идя по улице, я увидел открытые окна.
common_error.correct_alt: Когда я шёл по улице, окна были открыты.
common_error.explanation: A typical error for Spanish speakers is transferring the Spanish gerund to a construction where the subject does not match (in Spanish, 'Walking down the street, the windows were open' is acceptable, though sometimes considered incorrect). In Russian, the gerund requires its subject to be the same as that of the main clause. If there is no match, a temporal subordinate clause with 'когда' (when) or 'пока' (while) must be used. The solution is to reformulate the sentence or use a construction with 'когда'.

examples.translation: He was talking, smiling.
examples.note: Formed from the present tense of the imperfective verb (улыбаться → улыбаясь). Indicates an action occurring simultaneously with the main action.

examples.translation: Reading the newspaper, she was drinking coffee.
examples.note: Here 'читая' is the imperfective gerund of 'читать'. Used when the secondary action is ongoing as the main action occurs.

examples.original: Работая в саду, мы слушали музыку.
examples.translation: Working in the garden, we were listening to music.
examples.note: Observe that the gerund can be placed at the beginning or after the main clause without changing the meaning.

examples.translation: Having finished the work, he went home.
examples.note: From 'закончить' (perfective) comes 'закончив', indicating that the gerund’s action occurs BEFORE the main action.

examples.translation: Having seen me, she waved her hand.
examples.note: The verb 'увидеть' (perfective) gives 'увидев' (perfective gerund). If it were imperfective, it would be 'видя', but 'видя' is rare; 'увидев' is preferred.

examples.translation: Having prepared dinner, mom called the children.
examples.note: Use -в after a vowel in the root. General rule: infinitive ending in -ить, -еть, -ать (perfective) → -ив/-яв.

examples.translation: Not knowing the answer, he remained silent.
examples.note: Negation is formed with 'не' before the gerund. In Spanish, it translates as 'sin + infinitive' or 'al no + infinitive'.

examples.original: Будучи студентом, он работал по ночам.
examples.translation: Being a student, he worked at night.
examples.note: 'Будучи' is the irregular gerund of the verb 'быть' (to be). Used in formal or literary registers; in colloquial speech, 'когда был' is preferred.

examples.translation: He was reading, lying on the sofa.
examples.note: Some position verbs (лежать, сидеть, стоять) form gerunds used as adverbs of manner. They should not be confused with the active participle 'лежащий'.

title: Сослагательное наклонение (формальное) / Formal subjunctive
bridge: In Spanish, the formal subjunctive (like 'es esencial que él sea') expresses necessity, doubt, or evaluation. In Russian, there is no subjunctive mood as such; instead, the construction 'чтобы' followed by a verb in the past tense (the so-called Russian 'subjunctive mood') is used to express wishes, orders, or purposes. Additionally, the verb in the subordinate clause does not agree in person but remains in the past tense (or infinitive) depending on the context. This often confuses Spanish speakers, who expect an analogous subjunctive conjugation.
rule: In Russian, the expression of necessity, obligation, or evaluation is typically constructed with the word 'чтобы' (so that, in order that) followed by a verb in the past tense, regardless of the subject of the subordinate clause. This past-tense verb form is called the 'subjunctive mood' (сослагательное наклонение). Example: 'Важно, чтобы он пришёл' (It is important that he come). The verb 'пришёл' is in the past tense, but it does not indicate past time; instead, it expresses unreality or desire. To express 'it is essential that...', adjectives such as 'важно', 'необходимо', 'нужно', 'существенно' are used, followed by 'чтобы' and the verb in the past tense. There is no difference in person (he, you, we, etc.); all use the same past-tense form. Other common expressions: 'требуется, чтобы' (it is required that), 'желательно, чтобы' (it is desirable that), 'надо, чтобы' (it is necessary that). Be careful: if the verb in the main clause expresses will or command (demand, ask), 'чтобы' + past tense is also used. The infinitive is not used in these constructions, unlike some uses in Spanish.

concept_examples.text: Важно, чтобы он пришёл вовремя.
concept_examples.translation: It is important that he arrive on time.

concept_examples.text: Необходимо, чтобы все студенты сдали экзамен.
concept_examples.translation: It is necessary that all the students pass the exam.

concept_examples.text: Требуется, чтобы вы подписали документ.
concept_examples.translation: It is required that you sign the document.

concept_examples.text: Желательно, чтобы она позвонила нам завтра.
concept_examples.translation: It is desirable that she call us tomorrow.

common_error.explanation: The most common mistake is using the verb in the future tense ('придёт') instead of the past tense ('пришёл') after 'чтобы'. Spanish speakers tend to transfer the structure of the Spanish subjunctive, which often uses the present or future, but in Russian the 'чтобы' construction requires the past tense form (or infinitive in specific cases). Avoid conjugating the verb according to tense; remember that the past tense here indicates improbability or desire, not real time.

examples.translation: It is necessary that you come earlier.
examples.note: Notice that 'ты пришёл' (you came) uses the past tense, but the meaning is present/future.

examples.translation: It is important that we understand the rule.
examples.note: 'мы поняли' (we understood) does not indicate real past time, but a desired action.

examples.translation: I want you to help me.
examples.note: With verbs of desire (хотеть), 'чтобы' + past tense is also used.

examples.translation: It is necessary that you be careful.
examples.note: 'вы были' (you were) is used for all genders and numbers; agreement is made only in gender/plural, not in person.

examples.original: Существенно, чтобы проект был завершён в срок.
examples.phonetic: [sʊɕːɪstˈvʲitʲɪlʲnə | ˈʂtobɨ prɐˈɛkt bɨl zəvʲɪrˈʂon f srok]
examples.translation: It is essential that the project be completed on time.
examples.note: The verb 'был' (was) acts as an auxiliary in the past tense; the participle 'завершён' agrees in gender with 'проект' (masculine).

levels.label: Контраст с инфинитивом и временные нюансы
levels.translation: Contrast with the infinitive and temporal nuances

examples.original: Важно, чтобы каждый день выпивать стакан воды.
examples.phonetic: [ˈvaʐnə | ˈʂtobɨ ˈkaʐdɨj dʲenʲ ˈvɨpʲɪvətʲ stɐˈkan vɐˈdɨ]
examples.translation: It is important to drink a glass of water every day.
examples.note: When the subject of the main clause is impersonal, the infinitive can sometimes be used after 'чтобы' (less common than the past tense, but accepted).

examples.original: Он предложил, чтобы мы поехали на дачу.
examples.phonetic: [on prʲɪdˈloʐɨl | ˈʂtobɨ mɨ pɐˈjexəlʲɪ nɐ ˈdatɕʊ]
examples.translation: He proposed that we go to the dacha.
examples.note: If the main verb is in the past tense, the subjunctive can indicate a hypothetical or future action relative to that moment.

title: Будущее совершенное и будущее длительное / Future perfect and continuous
bridge: In Spanish, we use the future perfect (habré hecho) and the future continuous (estaré haciendo) to express future actions with nuances of completion or duration. Russian does not have equivalent compound tenses; instead, it uses constructions with adverbs, verb aspects (perfective/imperfective), and verbs of motion or state. The key is that in Russian, an auxiliary verb is not conjugated; instead, the correct aspect of the verb is chosen based on whether the action is completed or in progress, and temporal markers such as 'уже' (already) or 'всё ещё' (still) are added.
rule: In Russian, to express future perfect actions (equivalent to the future perfect), the perfective verb in the future (simple form, with prefixes) is used along with adverbs like 'уже' (already), 'к тому времени' (by that time). For the future continuous (equivalent to the future continuous), the imperfective verb in the future (conjugation ё/ешь...) is used, often with 'всё ещё' (still) or 'в течение' (during). There is no compound tense; the aspect (perfective vs. imperfective) is fundamental. Examples: 'Я уже напишу письмо' (I will have written the letter) vs. 'Я буду писать письмо' (I will be writing the letter). Note: the perfective future is formed with the present tense of the perfective verb (which already has a future meaning), while the imperfective future is formed with 'быть' (to be) + imperfective infinitive. It is also common to use constructions with short participles or adverbs for nuances of anteriority: 'к тому времени я закончу' (by then I will have finished).

concept_examples.text: К завтрашнему вечеру я уже закончу работу.
concept_examples.translation: By tomorrow evening, I will have already finished the work.
concept_examples.phonetic: k zavtrəʂnʲemu vʲetʃɪru ja uʐɨ zakɐnʲʨu rɐbotu

concept_examples.text: В семь часов я буду готовить ужин.
concept_examples.translation: At seven o'clock, I will be preparing dinner.
concept_examples.phonetic: v sʲem tɕisɐf ja budu gətɐvʲitʲ uʐɨn

concept_examples.text: К началу фильма мы уже купим билеты.
concept_examples.translation: By the start of the movie, we will have already bought the tickets.
concept_examples.phonetic: k nɨtɕəlu fʲilmɨ mɨ uʐɨ kupʲim bʲilʲetɨ

concept_examples.text: Он будет работать над проектом весь день.
concept_examples.translation: He will be working on the project all day.
concept_examples.phonetic: on budʲit rɐbotətʲ nət prɐjɛktəm vʲɛsʲ dʲenʲ

common_error.wrong: Я буду закончить работу к вечеру.
common_error.correct_alt: К вечеру я уже закончу работу.
common_error.explanation: The error lies in using 'буду + perfective infinitive' to express 'will have finished.' In Russian, the future of a perfective verb is formed with its simple conjugation (закончу), not with 'буду.' 'Буду' + infinitive is only used with imperfective verbs to indicate an action in progress or habitual. To avoid this mistake, remember that if you want to express that the action will be completed, you must use the perfective in the simple future; if you want to express that it will be ongoing, use the imperfective with 'буду'.

examples.original: Я напишу письмо к твоему приезду.
examples.phonetic: jɐ nəpʲiʂu pʲisʲmə k tvɐjɛmu prʲɪjɛzdu
examples.translation: I will have written the letter by your arrival.
examples.note: The verb 'написать' is perfective; its present form has a future meaning. It indicates a completed action in the future.

examples.original: Она уже прочитает книгу к пятнице.
examples.phonetic: ɐnɐ uʐɨ prətɕɪtɐjɪt knʲiɡu k pʲætnʲɪtsɨ
examples.translation: She will have already read the book by Friday.
examples.note: 'Прочитать' is perfective. The adverb 'уже' reinforces the idea of completion.

examples.translation: We will have arrived home by midnight.
examples.note: The perfective 'приехать' (to arrive) is used in the simple future, indicating completion.

examples.original: Завтра в десять утра я буду ехать на работу.
examples.phonetic: zavtrə v dʲɪsʲɪtʲ utrɐ jɐ budu jɛxətʲ nə rɐbotu
examples.translation: Tomorrow at ten in the morning, I will be going to work.
examples.note: 'Буду + imperfective infinitive' (ехать) expresses an action in progress at a future moment.

examples.translation: It will be raining all week.
examples.note: The verb 'идти' (to rain) in the imperfective infinitive with 'будет' indicates duration.

examples.original: Он будет готовить доклад всё утро.
examples.phonetic: on budʲit gətɐvʲitʲ dɐkɫat fsʲo utrə
examples.translation: He will be preparing the report all morning.
examples.note: Future imperfective with 'готовить' expresses a continuous action.

examples.original: К сентябрю я выучу русский язык, а сейчас я буду его учить каждый день.
examples.phonetic: k sʲɪntʲɪbrʲu jɐ vɨʊtɕʊ rusʲkʲɪj jɪzɨk, ɐ sʲɪjʨɪs jɐ budu jɪvo ʊtɕitʲ kɐʐdɨj dʲenʲ
examples.translation: By September, I will have learned Russian, and now I will be studying it every day.
examples.note: In the same sentence, we see the perfective (выучу – will have learned) and the imperfective (буду учить – will be studying). The context determines the aspect.

examples.original: Когда ты придёшь, я уже буду спать.
examples.phonetic: kɐɡdɐ tɨ prʲidʲoʂ, jɐ uʐɨ budu spatʲ
examples.translation: When you arrive, I will already be sleeping.
examples.note: The imperfective 'спать' with 'буду' is used to indicate an action in progress at a future relative moment.

examples.original: Она прочитает статью до обеда, а потом будет писать отчёт.
examples.phonetic: ɐnɐ prətɕɪtɐjɪt stɐtʲju dɐ obʲedɐ, ɐ pɐtom budʲit pʲisətʲ ɐtːɕot
examples.translation: She will have read the article before lunch, and then she will be writing the report.
examples.note: Contrast: 'прочитает' (perfective, completed) vs. 'будет писать' (imperfective, in progress).

title: Связки и дискурсивные маркеры для связности / Discourse markers for cohesion
bridge: In Spanish, we use connectors like 'sin embargo', 'por lo tanto' and 'además' to link ideas. In Russian, these markers serve similar functions, but they are often placed at the beginning of the sentence and may govern specific cases (for example, 'благодаря' requires the dative). Furthermore, some Russian markers (such as 'ведь') do not have a direct equivalent in Spanish and require a change in intonation or sentence structure. Pay attention to register differences: some are formal, others colloquial, and using them incorrectly can sound forced.
rule: Discourse markers in Russian are divided into several categories: additive (к тому же, кроме того), contrastive (однако, зато, а), causal (потому что, так как, из-за того что), consecutive (поэтому, следовательно, значит), and ordering (во-первых, затем, наконец). Some require a specific case for the preceding or following noun: 'благодаря' + dative (thanks to), 'из-за' + genitive (due to). In concessive phrases, 'хотя' + indicative verb is used. For contrast, 'а' is used for partial opposition and 'но' for strong opposition. To add information, 'также' usually comes after the verb, not at the beginning. To introduce a conclusion, 'итак' (so) is common in formal style. Regarding punctuation, they are usually preceded by a comma. Unlike Spanish, Russian discourse markers are not as easily omitted in formal registers.

concept_examples.text: Однако, результаты исследования были неожиданными.
concept_examples.translation: However, the research results were unexpected.

concept_examples.text: Из-за дождя мы остались дома.
concept_examples.translation: Due to the rain, we stayed at home.

concept_examples.text: Во-первых, прочитайте текст, а потом ответьте на вопросы.
concept_examples.translation: First of all, read the text, and then answer the questions.
concept_examples.phonetic: [vɐ‿ˈpʲervɨx prətɕɪˈtajtʲɪ ˈtʲekst | ɐ ˈpotəm ɐˈtvʲetʲtʲɪ nə vɐˈprosɨ]

concept_examples.text: Мы устали, поэтому пошли спать.
concept_examples.translation: We were tired, so we went to sleep.

common_error.wrong: Благодаря плохой погоды, мы не пошли гулять.
common_error.correct: Благодаря хорошей погоде, мы пошли гулять.
common_error.correct_alt: Из-за плохой погоды мы не пошли гулять.
common_error.explanation: The most common mistake is using 'благодаря' with the genitive case (as one would with 'из-за') and also confusing its meaning: 'благодаря' means 'thanks to', i.e., it has a positive connotation and requires the dative. To indicate a negative cause, one should use 'из-за' + genitive. The confusion arises because in Spanish 'gracias a' can be used positively, and 'por culpa de' negatively, but they are not as distinct in form. Remember: 'благодаря' + dative (positive cause), 'из-за' + genitive (negative cause).

examples.original: Кроме того, он хорошо играет на гитаре.
examples.phonetic: [ˈkromʲe ˈtovə | on xərɐˈʂo ɪˈɡrajet nə ɡʲɪˈtarʲe]
examples.translation: In addition, he plays the guitar well.
examples.note: 'Кроме того' is a formal additive connector, equivalent to 'además'. It is placed at the beginning of the sentence.

examples.translation: Another option can also be considered.
examples.note: 'Также' usually comes right after the verb or at the beginning, but always in a neutral register.

examples.original: Она умная, к тому же очень добрая.
examples.translation: She is smart, and moreover very kind.
examples.note: 'К тому же' adds an extra argument with a colloquial tone.

examples.original: Однако, экзамен был сложным, но мы справились.
examples.phonetic: [ɐdˈnɑkə ɪkˈzamʲɪn ˈbɨl ˈsloʐnɨm | nə mɨ sprɐˈvʲilʲɪsʲ]
examples.translation: However, the exam was difficult, but we managed.
examples.note: 'Однако' is formal and equivalent to 'sin embargo'. 'Но' is a simple contrast.

examples.original: Он не хочет идти, а я останусь дома.
examples.phonetic: [on nʲɪ ˈxot͡ɕɪt ɪˈtʲi | ɐ ja ɐˈstanʲʉsʲ ˈdomə]
examples.translation: He doesn’t want to go, whereas I will stay at home.
examples.note: The particle 'а' contrasts two actions and has no direct equivalent in Spanish.

examples.translation: But at least we rested well.
examples.note: 'Зато' introduces a compensation or a positive aspect.

examples.original: Он не пришёл, так как забыл о встрече.
examples.phonetic: [on nʲɪ prʲɪˈʂol | tɐk kak zɐˈbɨl ɐ ˈfstrʲet͡ɕe]
examples.translation: He didn’t come because he forgot about the meeting.
examples.note: 'Так как' is the most common form for 'because' in a neutral register, and it takes the indicative.

examples.translation: So I decided to wait.
examples.note: 'Поэтому' is used to indicate a consequence, often after the cause.

examples.original: Он плохо спал, следовательно, был невнимательным.
examples.translation: He slept poorly, therefore he was inattentive.
examples.note: 'Следовательно' is formal and equivalent to 'por consiguiente'. It is common in academic texts.

title: Язык дистанцирования / Language of distancing
bridge: In Spanish, we use structures like 'parece que', 'al parecer', 'tiendo a' or the conditional to distance ourselves from a statement. In Russian, this nuance is mainly expressed through modal adverbs (кажется, apparently), impersonal constructions with dative (мне кажется, it seems to me) and verbs with the suffix -ся (e.g., tendency to + infinitive). A typical error is to translate 'yo tiendo a' literally as 'я тенденцию', when in Russian the verb 'склоняться' with the dative case, or the construction 'у меня есть тенденция' (less natural), is used. Also be careful: while Spanish uses the subjunctive after 'parece que' in some contexts, Russian has no such mood; the indicative is used.
rule: In Russian, to express distancing or uncertainty (hedging), the following are used: 1) Modal adverbs: кажется (it seems), видимо (apparently), по-видимому (it seems), наверное (probably), возможно (possibly); they are placed at the beginning or before the verb, without changing the sentence structure. 2) Impersonal constructions with dative: мне кажется (it seems to me), ему казалось (it seemed to him), etc.; the verb 'казаться' is conjugated in the third person singular/plural according to the number of the logical subject, which is in the dative case. 3) Verbs of tendency: склоняться + inf. (to tend to), иметь тенденцию + inf. (less common), быть склонным + inf. They are used with the dative case for the person: я склонен (I am prone), она склонна (she is prone). 4) The particle 'бы' for conditional politeness or hypothesis: я бы сказал (I would say). There is no subjunctive; the indicative is used. For 'al parecer' one can use 'по-видимому' or 'как будто' (as if) with the indicative. In colloquial speech 'типа' (like) is used but it is informal. For B2 level, master impersonal forms and adverbs, and avoid direct calques of Spanish structures.

concept_examples.text: Кажется, завтра будет дождь.
concept_examples.translation: Parece que mañana lloverá.

concept_examples.text: Он склонен преувеличивать.
concept_examples.translation: Él tiende a exagerar.

concept_examples.text: По-видимому, они уже уехали.
concept_examples.translation: Al parecer, ya se han ido.

concept_examples.text: Я бы сказал, что это неплохая идея.
concept_examples.translation: Yo diría que es una buena idea.
concept_examples.phonetic: [ja by skɐˈzal ʂto ˈɛtə nʲɪpɫɐˈxajə ɪˈdʲejə]

common_error.correct_alt: У меня есть тенденция много говорить.
common_error.explanation: The error comes from translating 'tener tendencia a' literally as 'иметь + тенденция' in the accusative case, but in Russian the most natural form is the verb 'склоняться' (or the short adjective 'склонен') with the infinitive. 'Иметь тенденцию' can also be used but it is more formal and less common. Avoid direct calques and learn impersonal constructions with dative, which have no direct equivalent in Spanish.

examples.translation: Probablemente, él vendrá más tarde.
examples.note: 'Наверное' is used for probability; it is placed at the beginning or before the verb. No mood change is required.

examples.translation: Aparentemente, ella olvidó la cita.
examples.note: 'Видимо' indicates a supposition based on indirect evidence.

examples.translation: Posiblemente llegaremos tarde.
examples.note: 'Возможно' is equivalent to 'possibly' and is used with the indicative.

examples.translation: Me parece que es correcto.
examples.note: 'Мне' is the dative form of the personal pronoun; the verb 'кажется' is in the third person singular.

examples.translation: A él le parecía que ella bromeaba.
examples.note: The verb 'казаться' is conjugated in the past neuter singular for impersonal use.

examples.original: Нам показалось, что это слишком сложно.
examples.translation: Nos pareció que era demasiado difícil.
examples.note: Use of perfective 'показаться' for a one-time perception.

examples.translation: Ella es propensa al optimismo.
examples.note: 'Склонна' is the short feminine form; it is used with the dative (к + dative) or with the infinitive.

examples.translation: Tendemos a confiar en la gente.
examples.note: Short plural form 'склонны' + infinitive.

examples.translation: Él tiene tendencia a llegar tarde.
examples.note: More formal and less common form; 'иметь тенденцию + inf.' can be used.
